algorithms.name: Boundary Attack
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Origin of decision-based black-box attacks: walks randomly along the hard-label decision boundary while stepping toward the clean sample.
algorithms.summary_plain: Original label-only black-box attack that walks along the decision boundary from an adversarial start toward clean x.
algorithms.when_to_use: When benchmarking label-only models against the classic non-gradient random-walk baseline alongside HopSkipJump.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When gradients/scores are exposed or lowest possible query count is critical (use hopskipjump or square_attack).
extension_hooks: Swap Gaussian orthogonal proposals for DCT/Perlin priors for faster spatial convergence
Supply warm-start `x_init` from surrogate transfer or targeted class prototypes

algorithms.name: HopSkipJumpAttack (HSJA)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces random walk along the boundary with query-efficient Monte Carlo boundary-normal gradient estimation, geometric step-size search, and binary boundary projection.
algorithms.summary_plain: Label-only black-box attack that minimizes perturbation distance using binary search and Monte Carlo boundary gradient estimation.
algorithms.when_to_use: When you only observe final hard decisions (class labels) with zero access to gradients, probabilities, or logits.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When gradients or logit scores are available (use APGD/C&W/FAB or Square Attack for far lower query cost) or for continuous regression without decision boundaries.
extension_hooks: Swap isotropic Monte Carlo probes for frequency-subspace probes (QEBA)
Provide domain-specific x_init seeds for harder targeted attacks

algorithms.name: Natural Evolution Strategies Attack (NES)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces exact autograd backprop with antithetic Gaussian NES score-function gradient estimates using only forward queries.
algorithms.summary_plain: Estimates gradients from forward-only confidence queries via antithetic Gaussian search directions and runs PGD.
algorithms.when_to_use: Against non-differentiable or gradient-obfuscated models that still return continuous scores or logits.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When hard decisions only are exposed (use boundary or hopskipjump) or when white-box autograd works.
extension_hooks: Add time/data priors to Gaussian covariance -> Bandits-TD
Adjust search std `sigma` and `nb_sample` for noisy/stochastic RF channels

algorithms.name: Simple Black-Box Attack (SimBA)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Greedy +/- orthonormal basis probing over confidence scores without finite-difference gradient estimators.
algorithms.summary_plain: Greedy orthonormal-basis black-box attack that flips predictions by testing +/- single directions without estimating gradients.
algorithms.when_to_use: Minimalist query-efficient score-based baseline when simplicity and strict monotonic confidence reduction are desired.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Under strict hard-label-only access (use boundary or hopskipjump) or when gradients are available (use APGD).
extension_hooks: Substitute Cartesian unit basis with 2D-DCT or 1D-FFT orthonormal frequency basis (SimBA-DCT / SimBA-FFT)
Combine cosine/phase step scaling for complex wireless sub-carriers

algorithms.name: SPSA Black-Box Attack
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces exact autograd backprop with Rademacher simultaneous perturbation finite differences fed into projected Adam ascent.
algorithms.summary_plain: Gradient-free score-based attack that estimates ascent directions via random +/- probe pairs and updates with Adam.
algorithms.when_to_use: When models contain non-differentiable blocks (quantization, custom simulators) or to expose gradient masking when scores/logits are observable.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When only hard decisions are returned (use HopSkipJump), when strict query budgets are tight (use Square Attack), or when full gradients exist (use APGD).
extension_hooks: Swap Rademacher probes for spatial/burst random search -> Square Attack (ECCV 2020)
Switch from score queries to label-only queries -> HopSkipJump (IEEE S&P 2020)

algorithms.name: Square Attack
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Origin of query-efficient boundary random search: samples shrinking localized square patches (4D) or contiguous windows (1D/ND) without gradient estimation.
algorithms.summary_plain: Gradient-free score-based black-box attack that greedily proposes shrinking localized patches/bursts along the constraint boundary.
algorithms.when_to_use: Strongest general-purpose score-based black-box attack and essential sanity check against white-box gradient masking.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When only top-1 hard labels are observable without confidence/logit scores (use HopSkipJump).
extension_hooks: Chain with APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, and FAB -> AutoAttack
Customize patch geometry for frequency-domain or spectrogram bursts

algorithms.name: Zeroth Order Optimization Attack (ZOO-Adam)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces backpropagation in C&W with coordinate-wise symmetric finite differences and Adam updates using only output scores.
algorithms.summary_plain: Score-based black-box version of C&W that estimates gradients coordinate-by-coordinate via finite differences.
algorithms.when_to_use: When evaluating non-differentiable models that expose continuous logits/probabilities without gradient access.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When query budget is tight on high-dimensional images (prefer square_attack or nes).
extension_hooks: Add importance sampling over coordinate blocks for faster convergence
Tune penalty constant `const` or finite-difference step `fd_eps` per domain

algorithms.name: AutoAttack Ensemble
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Sequentially chains APGD-CE, APGD-DLR (untargeted + targeted), FAB, and Square Attack on surviving samples for parameter-free worst-case robustness.
algorithms.summary_plain: Sequential ensemble combining APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, FAB, and Square Attack to prevent single-attack blind spots.
algorithms.when_to_use: Final robustness benchmarking of any classifier when reliable worst-case accuracy matters across white-box and black-box regimes.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For fast inner-loop adversarial training steps or non-classification regression losses (use PGD/Adam-PGD).
extension_hooks: Adjust apgd_steps / fab_steps / square_queries for heavy full-benchmark runs
Use version='fast' to skip FAB when rapid screening is preferred

algorithms.name: Adam Projected Gradient Descent (Adam-PGD)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces raw sign/unit-L2 PGD updates with bias-corrected Adam first and second moment adaptive steps.
algorithms.summary_plain: Replaces fixed PGD steps with Adam's adaptive learning-rate transmission—especially effective on continuous signals and L2 power budgets.
algorithms.when_to_use: Continuous signals (wireless IQ, audio, sensor waveforms), regression losses, or L2/JSR-dB constraints where vanilla PGD oscillates.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When comparing strictly against standard Madry PGD or Croce & Hein APGD in CV classification benchmarks.
extension_hooks: Add cosine lr decay across steps
Combine with EoT random channel sampling for wireless fading robustness

algorithms.name: Auto-PGD Cross-Entropy (APGD-CE)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Adds parameter-free adaptive step-size halving at checkpoints w_j, rollback to best iterate, and momentum blending (alpha=0.75).
algorithms.summary_plain: Parameter-free strongest white-box PGD: automatically halves step sizes and rolls back to the best perturbation when progress stalls.
algorithms.when_to_use: Whenever you want maximum white-box attack strength without manually tuning step_size.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: If your model rescales logits so Softmax saturates to 0/1 (pair with or switch to apgd_dlr).
extension_hooks: Switch loss='dlr' to defeat Softmax gradient saturation -> APGD-DLR
Add stochastic environment expectations inside objective -> EoT-APGD

algorithms.name: Auto-PGD Difference of Logits Ratio (APGD-DLR)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Uses APGD Algorithm 1 with shift- and scale-invariant Difference of Logits Ratio (DLR) loss to eliminate Softmax gradient saturation.
algorithms.summary_plain: Scale-invariant Auto-PGD that defeats Softmax saturation and logit-scaling gradient obfuscation.
algorithms.when_to_use: Alongside APGD-CE on classifiers, especially if CE-based attacks unexpectedly stall with near-zero gradients.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Non-classification regression/MSE tasks without class logits (use APGD with a custom regression loss instead).
extension_hooks: Ensemble with APGD-CE, FAB, and Square Attack -> AutoAttack
Add EoT stochastic transforms for random wireless fading channels

algorithms.name: L1 Auto-PGD (Mind the Box)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Adapts Auto-PGD to sparse L1 threat models using exact box-intersected L1 projection and sparsity-scheduled steepest coordinate updates.
algorithms.summary_plain: Sparse L1-APGD: computes exact box+L1 projections and top-k steepest coordinate updates with adaptive step-size halving.
algorithms.when_to_use: Whenever evaluating sparse fixed-budget L1 robustness (fewer pixels/bins perturbed strongly rather than dense small noise).
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For dense L2/Linf perturbations or wireless JSR energy budgets (use apgd_ce, apgd_dlr, or sparsefool for unconstrained L0).
extension_hooks: Pass `loss='dlr'` against Softmax-saturated classifiers under L1 budgets
Customize top-k sparsity annealing schedule inside `_l1_steepest_step`

algorithms.diff_from_parent: Splits FGSM's single full step into multiple smaller iterative ascent steps with per-step projection (deterministic start at x).
algorithms.summary_plain: Deterministic multi-step iterative FGSM without random initialization.
algorithms.when_to_use: When you want a reproducible deterministic iterative baseline or to compare directly against FGSM without random-seed variance.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When testing models with sharp local gradient masking near x (prefer PGD with random_start=True or APGD).
extension_hooks: Add random start inside the ball -> PGD (Madry 2018)

algorithms.name: Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Origin of fast first-order gradient attacks: single-step linear ascent.
algorithms.summary_plain: Takes one full-budget step along the input gradient direction to rapidly probe linear vulnerability.
algorithms.when_to_use: Always run first as a 1-second sanity baseline and speed benchmark.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Never claim a model is robust solely because it resists FGSM; curved or masked loss surfaces easily fool single-step attacks.
extension_hooks: Add random initialization -> R+FGSM / Fast-FGSM
Iterate with small steps and projection -> BIM / PGD
Average gradient across random channel draws -> EoT-FGSM

algorithms.name: Momentum Iterative FGSM (MI-FGSM)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Accumulates an L1-normalized gradient momentum buffer (decay=1.0) across steps to stabilize update directions and boost transferability.
algorithms.summary_plain: Adds gradient inertia (momentum) across iterations to escape poor local optima and transfer better across unseen models.
algorithms.when_to_use: Primary baseline for transfer-based black-box evaluations (surrogate -> victim) and noisy/non-smooth loss surfaces.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For pure white-box worst-case evaluation on a single model, APGD or multi-restart PGD is usually stronger.
extension_hooks: Look ahead with Nesterov momentum -> NI-FGSM (Lin et al., ICLR 2020)
Combine with random input/channel transforms -> DI-FGSM / EoT-MI-FGSM

algorithms.name: Projected Gradient Descent (PGD)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces FGSM's single step with random initialization inside the ball, iterative small steps, and per-step projection (plus optional restarts).
algorithms.summary_plain: Randomly starts inside the allowed budget and iteratively climbs the loss surface while projecting back inside constraints.
algorithms.when_to_use: Primary white-box evaluation baseline for almost any differentiable model.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When the model contains non-differentiable steps (use SPSA/Square/HopSkipJump) or suffers from Softmax saturation (switch loss='margin' or use APGD-DLR).
extension_hooks: Accumulate gradient momentum -> MI-FGSM / NI-FGSM
Use Adam moment estimates instead of sign/L2 step -> Adam-PGD
Use adaptive step-size halving -> APGD-CE / APGD-DLR
Monte-Carlo sample random channel/environment transforms per step -> EoT-PGD

algorithms.name: Random-Start FGSM (R+FGSM)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Prepends a random step of size alpha (default 0.25 * eps) before computing the single-step FGSM gradient update of size (eps - alpha).
algorithms.summary_plain: Takes a small random hop to escape flat gradients near x, then executes one fast gradient step.
algorithms.when_to_use: Fast check against models showing suspiciously high FGSM robustness (e.g. adversarially trained or locally smoothed models).
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Not a substitute for full multi-step PGD or APGD when certifying strong white-box robustness.
extension_hooks: Continue iterating from the perturbed point -> PGD (Madry 2018)
Use multiple random draws and pick worst-case -> Multi-restart R+FGSM

algorithms.name: TRADES KL-Divergence PGD (TPGD)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Replaces supervised Cross-Entropy(y) loss with unsupervised KL(softmax(f(x)) || softmax(f(x_adv))) divergence maximization (TRADES inner adversary).
algorithms.summary_plain: Label-free TRADES adversary that maximizes KL divergence away from the model's clean prediction distribution.
algorithms.when_to_use: When ground-truth labels are unavailable, during TRADES robust training, or to test prediction stability on unlabeled streams.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For targeted class attacks or Softmax-saturated models where initial clean probabilities are one-hot (use apgd_dlr instead).
extension_hooks: Swap KL(p_clean || p_adv) with symmetric JSD or latent embedding cosine distance
Plug directly into TRADES outer training loss L_clean + beta * KL

algorithms.when_not_to_use: For fast single-batch evaluation or small sample counts without training overhead (use apgd_ce or uap).

algorithms.diff_from_parent: Lagrangian L2 + margin-hinge optimization with outer binary search over penalty constant c.
algorithms.summary_plain: Finds near-minimal L2/energy perturbations via Adam optimization over a smooth logit-margin objective and binary search.
algorithms.when_to_use: When measuring minimum jamming energy/distortion needed to break a classifier, or auditing defenses against gradient-based optimization.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When you need sub-second evaluation on huge datasets (use PGD/APGD/DeepFool first) or Linf-only threat models (use APGD/FAB).

algorithms.name: DeepFool
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Origin of geometric minimum-norm boundary attacks: iteratively projects onto the nearest linearized class hyperplane until misclassification.
algorithms.summary_plain: Finds a minimal perturbation to cross the nearest decision boundary via iterative hyperplane projection.
algorithms.when_to_use: When measuring the minimum distortion/power margin needed to flip predictions rather than testing a fixed epsilon.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For non-classification regression losses (needs class logits) or high-class-count outputs without max_classes capping (use C&W or FAB).
extension_hooks: Add biased boundary tracking & restarts -> FAB (Croce & Hein, ICML 2020)
Aggregate per-sample minimal vectors -> UAP (Moosavi-Dezfooli et al., CVPR 2017)

algorithms.name: Elastic-Net Attack (EAD)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Generalizes C&W L2 by adding an L1 regularization term beta * ||delta||_1 solved via FISTA soft-thresholding shrinkage.
algorithms.summary_plain: Optimizes Elastic-Net (L1 + L2) + C&W margin via FISTA shrinkage to craft sparse, transferable minimum-distortion attacks.
algorithms.when_to_use: When measuring minimum L1 or Elastic-Net distortion margins, or generating sparse perturbations that generalize well.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When fast fixed-budget evaluation suffices (use apgd_l1 or apgd_ce) or on non-differentiable models.
extension_hooks: Swap `decision_rule` between `'EN'` (Elastic-Net) and `'L1'` (strictest L1 minimum)

algorithms.name: Fast Adaptive Boundary Attack (FAB)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Improves DeepFool with biased forward projections toward x_clean (alpha_max), a backward contraction step (beta=0.9), and scaled restarts.

algorithms.when_to_use: When measuring exact minimal Linf/L2 robustness margins or building an AutoAttack-grade evaluation suite.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: For non-classification regression tasks without logits (use PGD/Adam-PGD with custom loss).
extension_hooks: Combine with APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, and Square Attack -> AutoAttack

algorithms.name: Jacobian Saliency Map Attack (JSMA)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Computes forward-derivative saliency S(x_i, t) combining target-logit sensitivity alpha_i and competing-logit sensitivity beta_i to perturb minimal feature counts.
algorithms.summary_plain: Greedy Jacobian saliency L0 attack that alters only the top few highest-leverage input features toward a target class.
algorithms.when_to_use: Low-to-medium dimensional tabular/sensor/image models when interpretable minimal feature-count (L0) tampering is studied.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: High-resolution ImageNet tensors (O(C * iter) Jacobians are slow; use sparsefool or apgd_l1) or complex-valued waveforms.
extension_hooks: Swap single-feature saliency lookup with pair-wise search for ultra-tight L0

algorithms.when_not_to_use: Against randomized or non-differentiable defenses without EoT/BPDA, or for minimum-norm boundary distance measurement.

algorithms.diff_from_parent: Averages Nesterov look-ahead gradients across m dyadic input amplitude scales x_nes / 2^i (Lin et al., ICLR 2020).
algorithms.summary_plain: Combines Nesterov look-ahead momentum with multi-scale gradient averaging (x / 2^i) to prevent surrogate overfitting.
algorithms.when_to_use: When transferring attacks across architectures or gain/amplitude regimes (images or linear wireless receivers).
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Against scale-sensitive preprocessing where amplitude halving collapses clean accuracy (set scale_copies smaller or use ni_fgsm/vmi_fgsm).
extension_hooks: Swap dyadic scaling `x / 2^i` with Admix image mixing or wireless SNR gain sweeps

algorithms.name: Translation-Invariant FGSM (TI-FGSM)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Convolves surrogate gradients with a symmetric 2D/1D smoothing kernel W (Gaussian/linear/uniform) to approximate translation-ensemble optimization.
algorithms.summary_plain: Convolves gradients with a Gaussian/smoothing kernel so perturbations are translation-invariant and evade defended victims.
algorithms.when_to_use: When transferring adversarial attacks onto adversarially trained models, CNN/ViT image models, or shift-sensitive 1D IQ/waveform models.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: On unordered tabular feature vectors where neighboring coordinates have no spatial or temporal adjacency.
extension_hooks: Swap smoothing kernel for a domain-specific bandpass/RRC filter in wireless RF jamming
Compose with DI-FGSM diversity and NI-FGSM look-ahead for SOTA black-box transfer

algorithms.name: Variance-Tuned MI-FGSM (VMI-FGSM)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Adds local neighborhood gradient variance tuning v_t across N random probes around each iterate.
algorithms.summary_plain: Samples N local neighbors per step to cancel surrogate gradient variance and boost black-box transferability.
algorithms.when_to_use: Strong domain-agnostic transfer attack when spatial transforms (DI/TI) do not apply or when attacking defended surrogates.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: Under ultra-tight runtime budgets where evaluating num_variance_samples extra gradients per step is too slow (use ni_fgsm).
extension_hooks: Add Nesterov look-ahead before g_t evaluation -> VNI-FGSM
Sample neighborhood perturbations along Rayleigh/phase manifold for complex wireless signals

algorithms.name: Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP)
algorithms.diff_from_parent: Aggregates per-sample minimal DeepFool boundary steps across a dataset into a single input-agnostic perturbation vector projected onto an eps ball.
algorithms.summary_plain: Learns ONE single input-agnostic perturbation vector that fools a model across almost an entire batch simultaneously.
algorithms.when_to_use: When evaluating streaming or real-time vulnerabilities (e.g., always-on wireless jammer or universal patch) where per-sample optimization is impossible.
algorithms.when_not_to_use: When sample-specific worst-case robustness is needed (use APGD or FAB), or for continuous regression without class decision boundaries.
extension_hooks: Replace sequential DeepFool aggregation with mini-batch EoT-SGD/Adam optimization
Condition universal vector on class labels for targeted UAP
